checks: Recenter at the symmetry center. For a shifted-strip section A, its reflection is an opposite strip section of the same body, and their Minkowski midpoint lies in the centered strip. Brunn–Minkowski gives the claimed volume comparison, including d=1 and the separate null-section case.

For a nonnegative mark projection a, the two tails sum to one minus the mass of the length-2a interval centered at t, minimized at t=0 by the strip comparison. For a negative a the complementary calculation gives one plus the length-2|a| strip mass, whose minimum is one by a finite shift outside the projection. Closed projection boundaries are null.

For every u the pair sum is at least 2f_K(y), using opposite caps to get f_K(y)≤V/2 in the negative branch. Setting t=0 before taking the infimum over u gives the reverse bound, even at exterior y. Conditioning on the independent symmetric shift and averaging its two signs yields the same pointwise floor after division by V, with no moment assumption.

overlap.comparison: Provides a dimension-dependent floor at the centroid for arbitrary convex bodies. This proof uses symmetry of the original body and obtains the exact off-center pair minimum and the pointwise depth floor for each arbitrary mark.
A nonsymmetric triangle shows that a weighted three-tail relation can fail after symmetric noise. That claim concerns another weighting and does not give the centrally symmetric pair identity.

readability: The displayed notation fixes the cap and mass conventions throughout.
review_method: Independent frozen proof read, exact algebra and rational geometry where applicable, accepted-fact comparison, and pinned source and dependency verification.

sources_verified.scope_verified: §§1–2 give the strip and both exact fixed-normal cases plus the ordinary-depth identity.
§3 gives the independent symmetric-noise floor at each deterministic point.

summary: The centered-strip comparison, exact fixed-normal and unrestricted paired minima, and pointwise symmetric-noise depth bound all follow with their stated scope.
